sensitiveAccessUnavailable: File, command and transfer access is unavailable while impersonating an owner.
title: Sandboxes

empty.title: No sandboxes yet
empty.description: Sandboxes start from a template on one of your hosts.
empty.deletedDescription: Destroyed sandboxes stay listed here with their history.
empty.activeDescription: Create a sandbox to start a VM from a template. Destroyed sandboxes are under Deleted.
empty.noMatchDescription: Check the spelling, or look under All if it was deleted.

filter.label: Show sandboxes
filter.name: Filter by name
filter.nameHint: Sandbox names use only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

stateHint.starting: The host is creating the VM. It shows Ready only after the host reports the guest ready.
stateHint.stopping: The host is stopping the VM. Nothing is final until the host reports it.
stateHint.stopped: The VM is off and its disk is kept. Start it again to use it.
stateHint.deleted: The VM and its disk are gone. Its history stays here.
stateHint.problem: The host could not keep this sandbox healthy. You can still destroy it.
stateHint.waiting: The pool is full. This create waits in line and starts when capacity frees up, or fails when its wait ends. It holds no host resources while it waits.

fields.noHost: No host (the sandbox has been removed from it)
fields.noHostWaiting: None yet (waiting in the pool queue)
fields.acceptedGrace: Disk kept after pool access loss

hostOffline: Host {{host}} is not connected ({{state}}). What you see may be out of date, and requested actions wait until the host is back.
hostQuarantined: Host {{host}} is quarantined: its inventory contradicts the server's records, so it accepts no new work until it reports a consistent inventory.

egress.title: Outbound network access
egress.openHint: The sandbox can reach public IPv4 destinations. Private networks, cloud metadata and the host's own addresses stay blocked.
egress.pending: Requested; fixed when the sandbox is placed.

reason.node_policy: Placed on another user's host whose owner allows only listed destinations for other users' sandboxes. Your fallback list applies.
reason.host_unsupported: This host's daemon can't enforce open internet yet; your fallback list applies.

egress.denyAll: Allowlist with no entries: all outbound traffic is blocked.
egress.domainsHint: Domain grants resolve to host-side IP destinations, not HTTP hostname or TLS identity isolation.
egress.domainsLapse: This is the list requested at creation, not a live view of what the host currently grants. The host grants each name's resolved addresses for a limited time and refreshes them while the sandbox runs; if a refresh fails, those grants lapse when they expire.
egress.immutable: Fixed at creation; the host re-verifies this policy before every start.
egress.fallbackHint: Unused while the sandbox has open internet. They apply only on a host that allows only listed destinations.
egress.deniedHint: The host's owner blocks these destinations, so this sandbox can't reach them.
egress.revoked: This sandbox had open internet on another user's host, whose owner has since stopped allowing it for other users' sandboxes. It can't start there again. Create a new sandbox.
egress.guardUnavailable: The host's network guard wasn't running, so the sandbox didn't start. Start it again once the host's owner fixes the guard.

hint.QUEUED: Waiting to be sent to the host.
hint.UNKNOWN_OUTCOME: The outcome is uncertain. The daemon retries stop and destroy automatically. Create and reconnect are not retried; check the sandbox state before acting again.
hint.FAILED: The host refused or failed this request.

lifetime.limitsFailed: Could not load lifetime limits. Try again to see all available choices.
lifetime.title: Lifetime
lifetime.startsAtReady: The lifetime starts when the sandbox is ready
lifetime.notAcknowledged: Not acknowledged by the host yet
lifetime.waiting: The lifetime starts when a host is assigned. Nothing runs while the create waits.

ack.pending: The host has not acknowledged the latest request, so the new lifetime is not guaranteed yet.
ack.differs: The host holds a different lifetime than the one requested.

hostExpiry.stopped: Confirmed {{when}}: the host stopped this VM when its lifetime ended (revision {{revision}}).
hostExpiry.deleted: Confirmed {{when}}: the host destroyed this VM when its lifetime ended (revision {{revision}}).

lifetime.hostEffectNotIssued: The host proved this VM was never created. Its capacity reservation has been released; destroy the sandbox to clean up.
lifetime.startNotIssued: The host did not start this sandbox, and nothing was changed. You can retry.
lifetime.hostDisconnectExpired: The host stayed disconnected past its carry limit, so it stopped this work. Check the sandbox before acting again.
lifetime.instanceMissing: The host reported that this VM no longer exists. Its disk may be gone; destroy the sandbox to clean up.
lifetime.expiryFailed: The host has not yet been able to enforce this sandbox's lease expiry and keeps retrying; capacity stays reserved until it confirms. Host reported: {{reason}}
lifetime.hint: Counted from when the server accepts your request; deployment limits apply.
lifetime.keepOverLimit: Keep its lifetime ({{lifetime}}): longer than this pool or host now allows
lifetime.keepUnlimitedOverLimit: Keep its lifetime (no time limit): this pool or host now requires a limit
lifetime.keepOverLimitHint: Its last lifetime is longer than this pool or host now allows, so choose one within the limit. A new choice becomes its lifetime for later starts. Counted when the server accepts your request.
lifetime.keepHint: It keeps the lifetime and expiry action it last had: from its create, its last start or its last renewal, whichever came last. Choose another to replace it; a new choice becomes its lifetime for later starts. Counted when the server accepts your request; deployment limits apply.
lifetime.destroyOption: Destroy the VM and its disk
lifetime.stopped: Not running: the lifetime starts again at the next start.

renew.title: Renew lifetime
renew.description: Choose how long it runs from now. What happens when it ends stays the same. Later starts keep this lifetime.
renew.shortenDescription: The new lifetime ends earlier than the current one ({{from}} → {{to}}). The sandbox stops sooner.
renew.doneStop: Lifetime renewed. It now stops at {{time}}.
renew.doneDestroy: Lifetime renewed. It is now destroyed at {{time}}.
renew.doneUnlimited: Lifetime renewed. It now has no time limit.

stop.title: Stop {{name}}?
stop.description: Stop shuts down the VM. A retained disk ends as Stopped so you can start it again.
stop.bootDescription: Stop interrupts boot. A retained disk ends as Stopped so you can start it again. If no instance was created, the sandbox ends as Deleted.

start.title: Start {{name}} again?
start.description: The VM boots from its kept disk and keeps its lifetime unless you choose another.
start.restoreDescription: Its disk is in the image store. Restoring downloads it to a host this sandbox may use, then boots it. It keeps its lifetime unless you choose another.

reconnect.title: Reconnect to this sandbox?
reconnect.description: Reconnect asks the host to check the running VM again. Use it when the terminal or files stop answering; nothing in the VM restarts.

destroy.recoveryDescription: The previous teardown outcome is unknown. Retry destruction to remove the VM and its disk. Capacity stays reserved until the host confirms deletion.
destroy.title: Destroy this sandbox?
destroy.description: The VM and its disk are deleted. This cannot be undone. To keep the disk, stop it instead.
destroy.waitingDescription: The create leaves the pool queue and the sandbox ends as Deleted. No VM or disk exists yet. This cannot be undone.
destroy.storedCopy: Destroy also deletes the stored copy of its disk in the image store.

rename.title: Rename sandbox
rename.description: Names are unique among your sandboxes. Renaming changes nothing inside the VM.
rename.label: Name
rename.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 63 characters. Unique among your sandboxes.

problem.notFound: This sandbox no longer exists or is not available to you.
problem.stateChanged: The sandbox changed state before this request arrived. The page shows its current state.
problem.keyReused: A different request was already sent for this action. Submit it again to send the new one.
problem.hostCapacity: The host has no free sandbox slot. Stop or destroy another sandbox on it, or raise its limit.
problem.hostDraining: The host is draining and accepts no new sandboxes.
problem.diskEvicting: The cached disk is being moved to storage. Start the sandbox again in a minute.
problem.restoring: The sandbox is being restored from storage. Try again once it is running.
problem.restoreNoAllowedHost: No host this sandbox may use has room for it right now. Try again later.
problem.hostDeleting: The host is being removed and accepts no new sandboxes.
problem.templateMissing: That host or template is no longer available.
problem.nameTaken: Another sandbox of yours already uses this name. Choose a different one.
problem.nameInvalid: That name is not allowed. Use 1–63 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, not starting with wssp-.
problem.egress: The outbound network entries were refused. Check the domains and CIDR ranges and try again.
problem.hostNoEgress: This host can't create sandboxes because it doesn't enforce outbound network rules. Its card on the Hosts page says what to check.
problem.egressGuardUnavailable: The host's network guard isn't running, so new sandboxes can't start there. Try another host or pool, or ask the host's owner to fix it.
problem.openEgressNotPermitted: The host's owner doesn't allow open internet for other users' sandboxes. Create a new sandbox, or turn off internet access and list the destinations it needs.
problem.invalid: The request was not valid. Check the values and try again.
problem.forbidden: This action is not permitted. Check your session and two-factor authentication.
problem.generic: The request failed. It may or may not have reached the server; trying again sends the same request.
problem.poolFull: All eligible hosts in this pool are full. Stop or destroy a sandbox, raise a host limit, or choose another pool.
problem.poolUnavailable: The pool's compatible hosts are disabled, offline, draining or awaiting launch verification. Enable or undrain a host, check its daemon, or choose another pool.
problem.poolIncompatible: No enabled host in this pool has a compatible runtime with outbound network rules. Check the member hosts or choose another pool.
problem.poolMissing: This pool does not exist or is not available to you. Choose another listed pool.
problem.hostUnavailable: This host is not ready for a new launch. Check its connection, inventory and image verification, then try again.
problem.imageMissing: The exact image is missing on this host. Restore the image and verify the revision again.
problem.createNotFound: The selected host, pool or template no longer exists or is not available to you. Refresh the picker.
problem.createForbidden: This pool has no active member hosts, or this action is not permitted. Check the pool members and your session.
problem.sizeInvalid: The VM size is invalid. Check the CPU count, RAM step and root-disk bounds.
problem.diskBelowImage: The root disk is smaller than this template's minimum disk (its image's own root). Choose at least the minimum, or leave the disk blank for the template's default.
problem.sizeUnsupported: The host or eligible group members cannot support this VM size. Choose a smaller size or another target.
problem.sizeMismatch: The stored allocation differs from the VM configuration. The operation needs investigation; its capacity remains reserved.
problem.capacityRam: Not enough free RAM on the host. Wait for a sandbox to stop, or ask the host owner to raise its limit.
problem.capacityVcpu: Insufficient total vCPU budget for this request.
problem.capacityDisk: No eligible storage pool has enough root-disk budget. Stopped sandboxes still retain disk commitments.
problem.capacityStorage: The original or eligible storage is unavailable or stale. Restore healthy storage; retained disks cannot move to another pool.
problem.capacityCeiling: The fixed retained-allocation guard is reached. Confirm deletion of unused roots before creating more.
problem.poolPolicyChanged: The pool grace decreased. Review the new quote before submitting again.
problem.shareQuota: Your shared pool resource cap is reached. Running RAM/vCPU and retained disks count toward the caps.
problem.memberQuota: This contribution’s RAM or vCPU percentage is reached.
problem.leaseExceedsPolicy: That lifetime is longer than this pool or host allows. Choose a shorter one.
problem.capacityReserved: Capacity is held for an older waiting request. Choose to wait, or try another pool.
problem.templateUnavailable: This template revision isn't on any host in this pool. Verify it on a member host or choose another template.
problem.queueFull: Too many creates are already waiting. Cancel one, or try again later.
problem.waitExceedsPolicy: That wait is longer than this pool allows. Choose a shorter one.
problem.diskUnavailable: The stored disk can't be used on this deployment right now. Ask an administrator to check the image store and the data encryption key.
problem.templateNotOnHost: This template isn't on that host. Choose another host or template.
problem.tunnelUnavailable: Preview links can't be used here: they are off on this deployment, or no host you can use runs them. Remove the preview ports, or choose another host.

detail.title: Sandbox
detail.notFoundDescription: It does not exist, or it is not yours.
detail.activityHint: Every lifecycle request, file transfer and command for this sandbox, with its result.

create.title: Create a sandbox
create.name: Name (optional)
create.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 63 characters. Leave blank for a generated name such as quiet-otter.
create.noHosts: You have no host that can run a sandbox yet.
create.noTemplates: You have no template you can use yet. Templates belong to your account: a pool shared with you doesn't share its owner's templates.
create.internetAccessOnHint: The sandbox can reach the public internet. Private networks, cloud metadata and the host's own addresses stay blocked. Fixed at creation.
create.fallbackSummary: Allowed destinations on hosts that block open internet
create.fallbackHint: Used only on such a host, where the sandbox runs in allowlist mode with these entries. Leave both empty to block all outbound traffic there.
create.egressHint: Only the destinations listed below are reachable; listing nothing blocks all outbound traffic. Fixed at creation.
create.egressDomainsHint: One domain per line, for example registry.example.com. Resolved on the host; subdomains are not implied.
create.egressCidrsHint: One range per line, for example 8.8.8.8/32.
create.done: Sandbox requested. It shows Ready once the host reports it.
create.hostWaits: This host isn't connected right now ({{state}}). A new sandbox needs a fresh connection and a verified image: reconnect its daemon, then create.
create.drainingHosts: Draining hosts accept no new sandboxes and cannot be chosen. Undrain one on the Hosts page.
create.selectorHint: Use its latest tag or pin an exact revision. The server checks compatibility at placement; changing placement keeps your selection.
create.revisionDiskHint: Default {{defaultDiskGiB}} GiB; at least {{minDiskGiB}} GiB (the image's own root). A larger disk grows the root filesystem on first boot.
create.latestSizeHint: The latest version's size is known only when you create. Pin a version under Template version to see its size here.
create.capacityWaitHint: Waiting keeps your place in line; the lifetime starts when the sandbox is placed. Destroy it to stop waiting.
create.guestSudo: Allow root for the guest user (sudo)
create.guestSudoOnHint: The guest user can run commands as root inside the VM with passwordless sudo. Commands, files and terminals still run as the guest user. Fixed at creation.
create.guestSudoOffHint: WS Sandbox Proxy gives the guest user no root. Fixed at creation.
create.guestRootTainted: Root may still be reachable in this template: this revision was built with root steps or captured from a sandbox that could run as root.
create.pageDescription: Pick a template and where it runs. Everything else has a safe default you can change under Advanced.
create.sectionTemplateHint: The image the VM boots. Its latest version is used unless you pin one under Advanced.
create.sectionPlacementHint: A pool picks its least-loaded host for you; a host runs it exactly there.
create.sectionBasicsHint: When the lifetime ends the VM stops and keeps its disk, unless you choose otherwise.
create.sectionAdvancedHint: Optional. Each line shows what will be used.
create.noPools: No pool is shared with you yet. Choose Host, or ask a pool owner to share one.
create.poolTrustLine: A shared pool may run your sandbox on someone else's host, and that host's operators can reach it.
create.offline: You're offline. Reconnect, then try again.
create.sizeIntro: Starts at the template's size. Leave a value alone to use the template's default.

capacity.hostMemory: This host has {{amount}} GiB of memory free.
capacity.hostDisk: This host has {{amount}} GiB of disk free.
capacity.poolCpu_one: The most any host in this pool can take now is {{count}} vCPU.
capacity.poolCpu_other: The most any host in this pool can take now is {{count}} vCPUs.
capacity.poolMemory: The most any host in this pool can take now is {{amount}} GiB of memory.
capacity.poolDisk: The most any host in this pool can take now is {{amount}} GiB of disk.
capacity.poolFailed: Couldn't check this pool's free capacity. The server still checks when you create.
capacity.poolNone: No host in this pool can take a new sandbox right now.
capacity.poolWaits: More than any host in this pool can take now: the create will wait for room.
capacity.hostLargest: Largest sandbox this host can take now: {{cpu}} vCPU · {{memory}} GiB memory · {{disk}} GiB disk.
capacity.hostUnknown: Connected, but this host hasn't reported its free capacity recently. The server checks when you create.

create.envHint: Private defaults for commands and terminals: up to 64 variables. HOME, SHELL and TERM are reserved. Values stay private on the server and host. Until the sandbox is created they stay only in this page (never saved in the browser), also after a refused create, and are gone when you leave it.
create.labelsRowsHint: Optional labels to find and group sandboxes: up to 32. Never put secrets here.
create.labelsTextUnavailable: Some keys can't be written as KEY=value lines; edit them as rows.
create.lifetimeHint: Counted when the server accepts your request. One hour by default; the host or pool may allow less.

templateOffHost.elsewhere: {{template}} isn't on {{host}}. Choose {{hosts}} or another template.
templateOffHost.nowhere: {{template}} isn't on {{host}}. Choose another host or template.
templateOffHost.warnElsewhere: {{template}} isn't on {{host}} yet, so creating there will likely fail. Choose {{hosts}} or another template.
templateOffHost.warnNowhere: {{template}} isn't on {{host}} yet, so creating there will likely fail. Choose another host or template.

create.previewPortsHint: Guest ports you may share later as a preview link, for example 3000, 8080. Leave blank if you don't need links; a port forward always works.
create.sizeNotSet: Not set: the latest version's own size is used.
create.labelKeyInvalid: {{key}} can't be a label name: no spaces, quotes or =.

draft.noHost: Choose a pool or an explicit host.
draft.name: Use 1–63 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens. The name cannot look like an ID or start with wssp-.
draft.templateOffHost: Choose an active template or revision from the loaded choices.
draft.lifetime: Choose a lifetime within the maximum this host or pool allows.
draft.labelsSyntax: Write each label as key=value on its own line, with no repeated key.
draft.labels: Labels allow at most 32 string entries: keys up to 64 UTF-16 units, values up to 1024, and 8192 UTF-8 bytes of JSON in total.
draft.egress: The outbound network entries aren't valid: one entry per line, at most 128 domains and 128 CIDR ranges.
draft.envs: Enter a valid environment map within the supported limits.
draft.unknownHost: That host is unavailable or draining. Choose a listed host.
draft.unknownPool: That pool is no longer listed. Reload or choose another pool.
draft.cpuCount: Enter a whole vCPU count from 1 to 32, or leave it blank.
draft.memoryMiB: Enter 0.5–64 GiB in steps of 0.25 GiB, or leave it blank.
draft.diskGiB: Enter a whole root size from 1 to 2048 GiB, or leave blank.
draft.credentials: Choose a login in every login row (each login once, at most 8), or remove the empty rows.
draft.previewPorts: Enter up to 8 different port numbers from 1 to 65535, separated by commas or spaces.

files.title: Files
files.description: Upload a file into the VM or download one from it, up to {{max}} each. Transfers use your signed-in session only.
files.unavailable: Files can be transferred only while the sandbox is Ready.
files.badPath: Enter an absolute path, such as /home/user/data.csv, without “..” parts.
files.receiptFailed: Could not read this transfer's status.

upload.title: Upload
upload.accepted: Upload accepted. Writing it into the VM: {{state}}.

download.title: Download
download.pending: Copying the file out of the VM: {{state}}
download.saved: Saving started. A prepared download can be saved once: prepare it again to save another copy.
download.failed: The host could not copy that file ({{state}}).

problem.tooLarge: The file is larger than this server allows.
problem.quota: Too many transfers are in progress. Wait for one to finish and try again.
problem.busy: The server is busy. Try again shortly.
problem.expired: This transfer expired. Start it again.
problem.forbidden: Your session can no longer transfer files here. Reload the page or sign in again.
problem.signedOut: You are signed out. Sign in again to transfer files.
problem.notFound: The sandbox or transfer no longer exists.
problem.notReady: The file is not ready yet.
problem.conflict: The sandbox changed state during the transfer. Nothing was replaced.
problem.storage: The server could not store the transfer. Try again later.
problem.invalid: The server refused the transfer request.
problem.cancelled: Upload cancelled. Nothing was written into the VM.
problem.uncertain: The upload was already being committed when it stopped, so the file may have been written into the VM. Check the sandbox's operations before trying again.

observations.livePage: One live page, up to {{limit}} entries. Refresh explicitly; later pages replace this page.
observations.entryDescription: Guest metadata observed for this page. Symlink targets are literal text, never followed.
observations.unavailable: Guest data is unavailable for this session or host.
observations.expired: This observation has expired. Refresh to request a new observation.
observations.stale: This identity or cursor belongs to an older sandbox generation. Refresh the list.
observations.unknown: The outcome is unknown. Guest work may remain alive. No command retry is available; stop or destroy the sandbox to recover.
observations.unsupported: The server or guest does not support this action.
observations.rateLimited: Too many actions. Dashboard and SDK keys share owner-wide budgets; wait before acting again.
observations.failed: The observation or control could not be confirmed.
observations.emptyFiles: This successful page contains no entries.
observations.emptyProcesses: This successful page contains no tracked commands.
observations.trackedOnly: Only commands started and supervised by WS Sandbox Proxy are listed. This is not a guest process census.
observations.argsTruncated: Some arguments were omitted from this bounded description.
observations.killDescription: Request canonical cancellation. Acceptance does not prove termination. An unknown outcome requires sandbox Stop or Destroy.
observations.killPrompt: Type the process ID to confirm
observations.alreadyExited: The command already exited before cancellation took effect.
observations.controlState: Control status: {{state}}. Acceptance is not proof of termination.
observations.connectDescription: Read the existing command and its retained output. Closing this dialog only detaches the observer.
observations.signalUnsupported: This guest does not support safe process group signals. No automatic kill was sent.
observations.processExited: The command has already exited. Refresh the process list.
observations.cancelPending: Cancellation is already pending. Acceptance is not proof of termination.
observations.processNotStarted: The command has not started yet. Refresh the process list.
observations.processUnavailable: The command is currently unavailable on its host. Refresh the process list.
observations.processMissing: This tracked command was not found for this process identity. Refresh the process list.

sharing.loss: Pool access lost. Guest IO is unavailable; disk deletion is scheduled no earlier than {{date}}. Restore a fitting access path before deletion commits to retain the disk. Offline cleanup may take longer.
sharing.restored: Access-loss deletion deadline cleared. A fresh start still checks current permissions, caps and the original disk; no restart is automatic.

capture.title: Save as template
capture.description: Capture this sandbox's disk into a new revision of a template.
capture.warning: Everything on the disk goes into the image, except what the scrub removes. Never save secrets in a template; images may be copied to hosts in shared pools if the template allows it. A running sandbox pauses for a few seconds.
capture.tagHint: The tag moves to the new revision. Lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore.
capture.scrubPathsHint: Optional. One absolute path per line, up to 16; added to the template's own list.
capture.invalidTag: Use 1–63 lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore, starting with a letter or digit.
capture.invalidPaths: Enter up to 16 absolute paths, one per line.
capture.minDiskHint: The new revision's minimum disk is this sandbox's disk ({{diskGiB}} GiB): a root never shrinks, so capture a sandbox created small to keep the template small.
capture.invalidDefaultDisk: Enter a whole size from {{diskGiB}} to 2048 GiB, or leave it blank for the source template's default.
capture.succeeded: Saved. The new revision is ready on the templates page.

problem.busy: A capture of this sandbox or on this host is already running.
problem.logins: A login is being installed, saved or recovered on this sandbox. Try again once it settles.
problem.unsupported: This sandbox can't be captured (its host, storage or state doesn't support it).
problem.policy: The template's image placement doesn't allow a capture on this host.
problem.quota: Your image store quota is full.
problem.store: The image store is unavailable; try again later.
problem.invalid: Check the tag, paths and disk size.
problem.defaultDisk: The default disk can't be smaller than this sandbox's disk.
problem.failed: Couldn't start the capture. Try again.
problem.offloaded: This sandbox's disk is only in the image store. Start the sandbox to restore it, then capture it.

capture.optionsSummary: Tag {{tag}} · {{disk}} GiB default disk · {{count}} extra paths

capacityWait.line: Number {{position}} in line · waits until {{deadline}} · blocked by {{blocker}}

credentials.heading: CLI logins
credentials.description: Logins installed in this sandbox. Attach one to install it now; free one to copy its tokens back and remove it.
credentials.stoppedHint: The sandbox is stopped: attaching records the login for the next start, and freeing ends it at once.
credentials.label: Attached logins
credentials.attachDescription: Pick a login. Leave the account and instance on “Any available” to let WS Sandbox Proxy choose a ready one.
credentials.freeDescription: Its environment variables leave new commands at once, its tokens are copied back, and its files are removed from the sandbox.
credentials.freeTerminals: Open terminals using it will close.
credentials.freeRevocation: Programs that already read the tokens may keep a copy; revoke them at the provider if that matters.
credentials.freeDiscardHint: “Free anyway (discard)” skips the copy-back: the stored value stays as it was, and any tokens refreshed in this sandbox are lost.
credentials.proxyHint: Proxied logins need the credential proxy, which is turned on only when a sandbox is created with a proxied login. Create a new sandbox that names this login.
credentials.ownHostsNote: Attaching a login keeps this sandbox on your own hosts from now on: its disk never restores onto another user's host.

connect.heading: Connect
connect.description: From a terminal where the wssp CLI is logged in with shell access:
connect.label: Connect commands
connect.sshSetup: For ssh, scp, rsync and editors such as VS Code, run this once (no SSH keys needed):
connect.getCliHint: Install it on your computer, then log in once:

connections.heading: Recent connections
connections.description: CLI shells, command channels and port forwards opened with an API key (wssp sandbox shell, wssp sandbox forward). Only who connected, when, which guest ports were forwarded and how much data moved is kept, for 90 days; never what ran.
connections.label: Recent connections
connections.empty: No CLI connections in the last 90 days.

onboarding.title: Get your first sandbox running
onboarding.description: Three steps. Each one is done once.

host.title: Enroll a host or join a pool
host.description: A machine you own, or a pool someone shared with you.
host.notReady: Your host is enrolled but can't take sandboxes yet: it isn't connected, or its egress guard isn't installed. Open Hosts to see what it needs.

template.title: Add a template
template.description: The image a sandbox starts from.

sandbox.title: Create a sandbox
sandbox.description: Start a VM from your template.
sandbox.waiting: Finish the steps above first: a sandbox needs somewhere to run and a template.

guestRoot.title: Root in the guest
guestRoot.pending: Requested; fixed when the sandbox is placed.

reason.node_policy: Root was requested, but this host's owner does not allow it in other users' sandboxes.
reason.host_unsupported: Root was requested, but this host's daemon can't grant it yet.

guestRoot.attested: The guest can run as root, so command results are reported by the guest itself, and a command whose outcome is unknown is cleared only when the host sees the VM stop or restart.
guestRoot.identity: Commands, files and terminals run as the guest user. Fixed at creation.
guestRoot.revoked: This sandbox had root (sudo) on another user's host, whose owner has since stopped allowing it. It can't start there again. Create a new sandbox.

restoreOverride.hint: The SDK key that created this sandbox limits where it may restore, and none of those hosts had room.
restoreOverride.title: Restore outside the creating key's hosts?
restoreOverride.description: The SDK key that created this sandbox will lose access to it. Access follows the sandbox's current host, and the new host is outside that key's allowlists. You keep full access from the dashboard.

restoreLoginWait.inUse: The restore waited, but every matching login instance stayed in use. Stop a sandbox that holds one or add an instance, then start again.
restoreLoginWait.busy: The restore waited, but a login it needs stayed held by a running sandbox or a login session. Start again once it is free, or check it on the CLI logins page.
restoreLoginWait.pendingDrain: The restore waited, but a login it needs was still being released elsewhere. Start again in a moment.
restoreLoginWait.needsLogin: The restore waited, but no matching login instance was ready. Log in or upload a value on the CLI logins page, then start again.
restoreLoginWait.accountPaused: The restore waited, but a login account it needs stayed paused. Resume the account on the CLI logins page, then start again.
restoreLoginWait.limitReached: The restore waited, but a login limit stayed reached. Free a login instance or raise the limit, then start again.
restoreLoginWait.hostForbidden: The restore waited, but no host with room may hold an attached login. Check the login's host settings on the CLI logins page, then start again.
restoreLoginWait.recoveryRequired: The restore waited, but a login it needs must be recovered first. Check the login on the CLI logins page, then start again.

locationHint.host: The disk exists only on the host that runs it.

locationHint.store: The disk is only in the image store. Starting the sandbox restores it onto a host it may use.

failure.quota_exceeded: The account's stored-disk quota is used; the disk stays on its host.

policy.title: When should a stopped disk go to the store?
policy.description: Copying a stopped disk to the image store lets its host free the space and lets the sandbox start on another host. A disk not yet copied is only on its host: if that host is lost, the disk is lost.

option.on_stopHint: The default. The disk is copied in the background after every stop.
option.afterHint: The disk is copied only once the sandbox has been stopped this long. A start before then copies nothing.
option.on_pressure: Only when its host needs the space
option.on_pressureHint: Keep the disk on its host. Use this to park a sandbox you expect to start again.

policy.minutesHint: Counted from the stop. 1 minute to 24 days.
policy.minutesInvalid: Enter a whole number of minutes from {{min}} to {{max}}.
policy.pressure: Whatever you choose, a host that needs the space (draining with offload, nearly full, or blocking new sandboxes for lack of disk) copies stopped disks to the store early.
policy.failed: Couldn't save the offload setting. Try again.

displayHint.STARTING: The host is booting the VM from its kept disk. It shows Ready once the guest reports ready.
displayHint.RESTORING: The host is downloading the stored disk and booting the VM. It shows Ready once the guest reports ready.
displayHint.DESTROYING: The host is deleting the VM and its disk. Nothing is final until the host reports it.
